edges.description: In an affected child, acute kidney failure at age 3 was attributed to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and resolved after they were stopped.
Overexpression of mutant renin disturbs convolution of the pronephric tubules in most injected embryos.
edges.limitations: Overexpression of a human mRNA in wild-type embryos rather than a heterozygous germline allele; the embryonic pronephros cannot show the slowly progressive fibrosis, endocrine defects or anemia of the human disease.
edges.source: Zebrafish embryos injected with human L381P renin mRNA

edges.description: Loss of juxtaglomerular cells lowers renin expression, plasma renin and blood pressure, followed by vascular abnormalities and striped fibrosis.
edges.limitations: Juxtaglomerular cells are lost through loss of microRNA processing, not through a toxic REN variant, so the model informs only the consequences of renin-cell loss and says nothing about how REN variants cause it.

nodes.description: The mutant precursor fails to follow the normal secretory route. Signal peptide variants leave unprocessed, non-glycosylated preprorenin in the cytoplasm; prosegment variants accumulate in the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi intermediate compartment; mature-peptide variants are retained in the endoplasmic reticulum.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and molecular characterization of a family with a dominant renin gene mutation and response to treatment with fludrocortisone.
evidence.snippet: The mutation affects endoplasmic reticulum co-translational translocation and posttranslational processing, resulting in massive accumulation of non-glycosylated preprorenin in the cytoplasm.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease with Adult Onset due to a Novel Renin Mutation Mapping in the Mature Protein.
evidence.snippet: Expression of the L381P variant leads to its ER retention and induction of the Unfolded Protein Response in cell models

nodes.description: A presenting feature in about 10% of patients with signal peptide variants; nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and dehydration are recognized precipitants.

evidence.reference_title: An international cohort study of autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to REN mutations identifies distinct clinical subtypes.
evidence.snippet: Only patients in the signal group presented with acute kidney injury (10%) or acidosis, anemia, and kidney failure (13%).

nodes.description: Lifelong urate-lowering therapy to prevent gout.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease – REN.
evidence.snippet: In all persons with ADTKD-REN, lifelong treatment of hyperuricemia with allopurinol prevents gout.

nodes.description: Hypoproliferative anemia in the first decade, present in childhood in 91% of patients with signal peptide variants and 69% with prosegment variants, and absent with mature-peptide variants. Mean hemoglobin in untreated children was about 10 g/dL.

evidence.reference_title: An international cohort study of autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to REN mutations identifies distinct clinical subtypes.
evidence.snippet: Anemia was present in childhood in 91% in the signal group, 69% prosegment, and none of the mature group.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease with Adult Onset due to a Novel Renin Mutation Mapping in the Mature Protein.
evidence.snippet: ADTKD-REN is characterized by hypoproliferative anemia with low hemoglobin concentration in the first decade of life

nodes.description: Slowly progressive with a bland urine sediment. Signal peptide and prosegment variants often present in childhood or adolescence; mature peptide variants present in adulthood.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease – REN.
evidence.snippet: Childhood/adolescent onset, the more common presentation (caused by REN variants encoding the signal peptide or prosegment domains), is characterized by decreased estimated glomerular filtration rate, acidosis, hyperkalemia, and anemia early in life, followed by slowly progressive chronic kidney disease (CKD) and gout.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and molecular characterization of a family with a dominant renin gene mutation and response to treatment with fludrocortisone.
evidence.snippet: A random plasma renin activity was < 0.5 ng/ml/h (normal 0.5 – 5.9 ng/ml/h) with a random serum aldosterone measurement < 4.0 ng/dl at age 10 years (normal 4 – 31 ng/dl).

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and molecular characterization of a family with a dominant renin gene mutation and response to treatment with fludrocortisone.
evidence.snippet: A random plasma renin activity was < 0.5 ng/ml/h (normal 0.5 – 5.9 ng/ml/h) with a random serum aldosterone measurement < 4.0 ng/dl at age 10 years (normal 4 – 31 ng/dl).

nodes.description: Hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis replaces kidney function at kidney failure.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease – REN.
evidence.snippet: Renal replacement therapies (such as hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis) can replace renal function, but are associated with potential complications.

nodes.description: Mutant renin activates the unfolded protein response (BiP induction, XBP1 splicing and the ATF6 branch for p.Leu381Pro). This is not universal: the signal peptide variant p.Trp17Arg did not activate endoplasmic reticulum stress in a cell model and was instead routed to mitochondria.

nodes.description: Erythropoiesis-stimulating therapy for the childhood anemia, which responds to erythropoietin but not to iron.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant mutation in the signal peptide of renin in a kindred with anemia, hyperuricemia, and CKD.

nodes.description: Mineralocorticoid replacement for hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism. It corrects mild hypotension, hyperkalemia and acidemia, and raised eGFR in an affected child; in the international cohort it lowered serum potassium and raised bicarbonate without reported adverse effects. GeneReviews suggests it may be indicated before stage 3 chronic kidney disease.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease – REN.
evidence.snippet: Fludrocortisone (a pharmacologic analog of aldosterone) corrects aldosterone deficiency (and associated mild hypotension), hyperkalemia, and acidemia.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and molecular characterization of a family with a dominant renin gene mutation and response to treatment with fludrocortisone.
evidence.snippet: Treatment with fludrocortisone in an affected 10-year-old child resulted in an increase in blood pressure and estimated glomerular filtration rate.

evidence.reference_title: An international cohort study of autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease due to REN mutations identifies distinct clinical subtypes.
evidence.snippet: Fludrocortisone raises eGFR, lowers serum potassium, and improves serum bicarbonate, but only a few patients received treatment with this medication, limiting our abilities to understand advantages and disadvantages of treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Case-inspired exploration of renin mutations in autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease: not all paths lead to the endoplasmic reticulum.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, fludrocortisone treatment has shown efficacy in stabilizing the renal function of our patient over a four-year period without significant side effects.

nodes.description: Developed in more than half of patients in every variant group, with a mean age at first attack in the late twenties to early thirties; the usual presenting feature of mature-peptide variants.

evidence.snippet: Patients in the mature group presented only with gout (75%) or CKD (25%).

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease – REN.
evidence.snippet: Childhood/adolescent onset, the more common presentation (caused by REN variants encoding the signal peptide or prosegment domains), is characterized by decreased estimated glomerular filtration rate, acidosis, hyperkalemia, and anemia early in life, followed by slowly progressive chronic kidney disease (CKD) and gout.

nodes.description: Germline heterozygous missense variants and single-residue in-frame deletions in REN. About 60% affect the signal peptide (for example p.Leu16del, p.Leu16Arg, p.Trp10Arg, p.Cys20Arg), about 25% the prosegment and about 15% the mature renin peptide (for example p.Leu381Pro). The mutant protein is thought to be toxic to renin-producing cells in addition to lowering renin output.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant renin gene mutations associated with early-onset hyperuricemia, anemia, and chronic kidney failure.
evidence.snippet: we identified three unrelated families with the autosomal-dominant inheritance of early onset anemia, hypouricosuric hyperuricemia, progressive kidney failure, and mutations resulting either in the deletion (p.Leu16del) or the amino acid exchange (p.Leu16Arg) of a single leucine residue in the signal sequence of renin.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease with Adult Onset due to a Novel Renin Mutation Mapping in the Mature Protein.
evidence.snippet: Through exome sequencing in an adult-onset ADTKD family we identified a new renin variant, p.L381P, mapping in the mature protein.

genetic_context.description: Germline heterozygous missense variants and in-frame single-codon deletions, inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.

nodes.description: Mild and rarely life-threatening; absent with mature-peptide variants.

nodes.description: Reduced urine concentrating ability from childhood.

nodes.description: Low fractional excretion of uric acid.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and molecular characterization of a family with a dominant renin gene mutation and response to treatment with fludrocortisone.
evidence.snippet: The serum uric acid was elevated at 375 umol/l (6.3 mg/dl) (normal range 107 – 315 umol/l), with a fractional excretion of uric acid (FEurate) 5.2% (normal 6 – 20%).

nodes.description: Relative hypotension and volume contraction increase proximal tubular sodium and, with it, urate reabsorption, so the fractional excretion of uric acid is low. This is the proposed basis of hypouricosuric hyperuricemia.

evidence.reference_title: Discovery of a novel dominant mutation in the REN gene after forty years of renal disease: a case report.
evidence.snippet: This relative hypotension stimulates the reabsorption of sodium in the proximal tubule, which consequently leads to an increase in urate reabsorption and hyperuricaemia.

nodes.description: Curative for the kidney disease because the transplanted kidney does not develop the disorder. Related living donors should first be tested for the familial variant.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease – REN.
evidence.snippet: Kidney transplantation is curative, as the transplanted kidney does not develop the disease.

nodes.description: The mutant protein is proposed to exert a dominant toxic effect that gradually reduces the viability of renin-expressing juxtaglomerular cells. Kidney biopsies show reduced renin and renin-angiotensin system component expression and a juxtaglomerular apparatus that is not prominent.

nodes.description: Leader peptide and prosegment variants send mutant preprorenin fully (for example p.Leu16Arg, p.Trp17Arg, p.Cys20Arg) or partly (p.Trp10Arg, p.Leu16del) into mitochondria, with a mitochondrial import defect and fragmentation of the mitochondrial network. This offers an alternative to endoplasmic reticulum stress for variants that do not activate the unfolded protein response.

evidence.reference_title: Leader peptide or pro-segment mutants of renin are misrouted to mitochondria in autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease.
evidence.snippet: The mutated pre-pro-sequence of renin is necessary and sufficient to drive mitochondrial rerouting, mitochondrial import defect and fragmentation.

evidence.snippet: Notably, the W17R variant was misrouted to the mitochondria resulting in changes of the mitochondrial network organisation.

nodes.description: Erythropoietin levels are low or inappropriately normal for the degree of anemia, which is disproportionate to the reduction in kidney function and responds to erythropoietin but not to iron.
